title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 400
paragraphs: The following story is also told, which for my part I do not believe — that one of the Persian women came in to visit the wives of Cyrus, and when she saw children of comely form and tall standing by Cassandane's side, she loudly praised them and expressed great admiration; and Cassandane, who was the wife of Cyrus, said: “Nevertheless, though I am the mother of such children as these, Cyrus treats me with dishonor and holds in honor the woman he has brought in from Egypt.” Thus she spoke, they say, being vexed by Nitetis, and upon that Cambyses, the elder of her sons, said: “For this reason, mother, when I am grown to be a man, I will turn what is above in Egypt to below and what is below to above.” He is reported to have said this when he was perhaps about ten years old, and the women were astonished at it. He, they say, always kept it in mind, and so at last, when he had become a man and had obtained royal power, he made the expedition against Egypt.
